title: Three Nights and One Short Script
subtitle: 戏剧表演 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 戏剧表演（文学艺术与体育·戏剧与表演）
meta: 主题语境：戏剧表演（文学艺术与体育·戏剧与表演）　|　核心词汇：trick　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 trick 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1971 the director ① played the trick that no actor in the theatre would have described, and he said the playing was the whole of the night. The ② trick, meaning the device itself and not the script, ran three nights and stayed undescribed in the book; a trick, he said, is the only thing in a theatre that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ trick in that theatre had the same short script beside it, and the ④ trick at the far stage, meaning the prop they kept for the children to move and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A trick, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the director said the describing is the part that fills three nights.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the trick was the whole of the matter, meaning the wit and not the device. The ⑥ trick, meaning the wit and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; trick, he said, is either something you play or the only word that means both a device and a wit. He said the wit is the part they remember.

By 1976 the ⑦ trick had become a line in a poster, and the poster had become an argument about the short script. The ⑧ trick of the whole thing, the director wrote in August, was one theatre and three nights of describing; trick, he said, is either the prop at the far stage or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ trick I remember is the device described in the poster, which closed in 1978 and is still described as the quietest in the theatre. A ⑩ trick, my mother said in 1980, is the only device that improves by being described; every trick, she said, is a wit that has agreed to look like a device. She said the wit was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 诡计；戏法（指戏院里每一个旁边的那一个）
B. n. 诡计；戏法（指那个诡计本身，与薄薄的剧本相对）
C. 固定搭配：play the trick 耍这一个诡计
D. n. 诡计；戏法（指留给孩子们搬的那一件）
E. n. 诡计之事（抽象总称，指一处戏院的诡计之事）
F. n. 诡计；戏法（指戏报里写到、被描述的那一个）
G. n. 诡计、巧思（指一件事里人人都看却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 巧思（抽象总称，指人人都看却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: played the trick that no actor in the theatre would have described
The trick, meaning the device itself and not the script
the trick at the far stage
the trick was the whole of the matter
the trick had become a line in a poster
The trick of the whole thing
A trick, my mother said in 1980

answers.why: play the trick 意为“耍这一个诡计”，1971 年那位导演把戏院里没有一位演员肯描述的一个诡计做了一遍。
trick 意为“诡计；戏法”，指那个诡计本身而不是薄薄的剧本，它经过了三个夜晚而在簿子上没有被描述。
trick 意为“诡计；戏法”，指戏院里每一个旁边的那一个，每一个旁边都有同一册薄薄的剧本。
trick 意为“诡计；戏法”，指最远那处台口的留给孩子们搬的那一件，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
trick 意为“诡计、巧思”，指一件事里人人都看却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这个巧思就是那件事的全部。
trick 意为“巧思”，指人人都看却无人提起的那样东西而不是那个诡计，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
trick 意为“诡计；戏法”，指戏报里写到、被描述的那一个，到 1976 年这一个成了戏报里的一行。
trick 意为“诡计之事”，导演八月写道，整件事的诡计之事是一处戏院和三个夜晚的描述。
trick 意为“诡计；戏法”，我记得的是戏报里描述过的那一个，1978 年演完了，至今仍被说成戏院里最安静的一个。
trick 为抽象总称，母亲 1980 年说，诡计是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的诡计。
